content:
The Numbers chapter is a dependable source of marks in the CTET Paper I (Classes I–V) Mathematics section — and it is one you can master quickly with the right practice. This guide explains what CTET numbers place value actually tests, the facts and formulas worth memorising, the mistakes that quietly cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now to check where you stand.

Work through the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter-test e-book at the end for full, exam-style practice. That "test → review → practise" loop is how serious CTET candidates turn a weak topic into a strong one.

What Numbers covers in CTET Paper I Maths

At the primary level this chapter blends content knowledge with pedagogy — how young children learn the idea. Expect questions on:

  • Place value and expanded form
  • Number names and Roman numerals
  • Comparing and ordering numbers
  • Odd and even numbers, successor and predecessor

Practise the full syllabus free on the CTET Paper I Mathematics course at vidaara.org, then test yourself here.

Key facts and formulas to remember

  • In 234, the digit 2 has a place value of 200 (2 hundreds).
  • Expanded form of 234 is 200 + 30 + 4.
  • Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6, 8; odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
  • Roman numerals: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Confusing a digit's face value with its place value.
  • Comparing numbers digit-by-digit from the wrong (units) end.

quiz.title: CTET Numbers Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper I – pattern questions on Numbers. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: The sum of three consecutive natural numbers is 72. What is the largest of these three numbers?
questions.explanation: Let the three consecutive numbers be n-1, n, n+1. Sum = (n-1) + n + (n+1) = 3n. Given 3n = 72, so n = 24. The numbers are 23, 24, 25. The largest is 25. Alternatively, middle number = 72 ÷ 3 = 24, so largest = 25.

questions.q: A teacher writes the numbers 789, 798, 879, 897 on the board and asks for the descending order. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: Descending means largest to smallest. All have 3 digits. Compare hundreds: 8,8,7,7. 897 and 879 are larger. Compare tens of 897 (9) and 879 (7): 9 > 7, so 897 > 879. Next come 798 and 789. Tens: 9 > 8, so 798 > 789. Full order: 897, 879, 798, 789.

questions.q: What is the Hindu-Arabic numeral for the Roman numeral 'XIX'?
What does the digit '5' represent in the number 15,268?
questions.explanation: The number is 1,52,68 in the Indian system, but the place value is universal. The places are: 1-Ten Thousands, 5-Thousands, 2-Hundreds, 6-Tens, 8-Ones. The digit 5 is in the Thousands place, so its value is 5 × 1000 = 5000 (5 thousands).

questions.q: Which of the following numbers is represented by the expansion (3 × 1000) + (0 × 100) + (2 × 10) + (9 × 1)?
What is the expanded form of the number 7043?
questions.explanation: The place values are: 7 Thousands = 7000, 0 Hundreds = 0, 4 Tens = 40, 3 Ones = 3. The correct expanded form is 7000 + 0 + 40 + 3.

questions.q: The number four thousand six hundred nine in standard form is:
questions.explanation: Four thousand = 4000, Six hundred = 600, Nine = 9. Sum = 4000 + 600 + 9 = 4609. There are no tens mentioned, so the tens place is 0.

questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE about the numbers 80,809 and 88,090?
questions.explanation: Both are 5-digit numbers. Compare the ten-thousands place: 8 = 8. Compare the thousands place: 0 in 80,809 vs 8 in 88,090. Since 0 < 8, we have 80,809 < 88,090.

questions.q: The difference of 'XC' and 'XX' in Hindu-Arabic numerals is:

faq.a: Place value is the value a digit has because of its position — in 345 the 3 means 300, the 4 means 40 and the 5 means 5.

faq.q: How do you compare two numbers?
faq.a: First compare how many digits each has; if equal, compare digit by digit from the highest (left-most) place.
